seoTitle: How to Publish Your Indicator on TradingView
metaDescription: Learn how to publish a Pine Script indicator on TradingView, choose public or invite-only visibility, and avoid common script publishing errors.
intro: If you've built your own Pine Script indicator, sharing it with the TradingView community involves more than just clicking publish. This guide covers how to prepare your script, open the publish option, choose between public and invite-only visibility, and add the right description and tags. It's aimed at Pine Script beginners and developers ready to share their work.

steps.heading: Prepare your indicator script
steps.body: Make sure your Pine Script code is clean, functional, and free of errors before attempting to publish it.

steps.heading: Open the Publish Script option
steps.body: From the Pine Editor, locate the publish option to begin the process of sharing your script.

steps.heading: Choose public or invite-only visibility
steps.body: Decide whether you want your script open to everyone or restricted to specific invited users.

steps.heading: Add a proper title, description, and tags
steps.body: Write a clear title and description explaining what your indicator does, and add relevant tags to help others find it.

steps.heading: Submit and fix common publishing errors
steps.body: Submit your script for publishing, and address any error messages related to formatting, naming, or content guidelines if they appear.

faq.question: What's the difference between public and invite-only scripts?
faq.answer: Public scripts are visible to any TradingView user, while invite-only scripts are restricted to users you specifically grant access to.

faq.question: Do I need to write a detailed description before publishing?
faq.answer: Yes, TradingView typically expects a clear description explaining what the indicator does and how to use it before allowing publication.

faq.question: Why might my script fail to publish?
faq.answer: Common issues include incomplete descriptions, code that doesn't meet formatting guidelines, or missing required details in the submission.

faq.question: Can I edit my indicator after it's published?
faq.answer: Yes, you can typically make updates to a published script, though changes may need to go through a review process again.
